title: Harbor clinic scheduling workspace
audience: Front-desk staff coordinating appointments across clinicians
scenario: Harbor is a static daily schedule view for a community clinic. Patient names are intentionally fictional.
task: Build an accessible scheduling workspace that makes appointment status, time, clinician, and room easy to scan without implementing scheduling actions.

sections: Application navigation with Schedule, Patients, Messages, Reports, and Settings
Day header with Previous day, Today, Next day, and New appointment controls
Clinician columns for Dr. Imani, Dr. Patel, and J. Flores NP
Appointments for Alex Kim at 09:00, Robin Wells at 09:30, Casey Hall at 10:15, and Morgan Lee at 11:00
Statuses Checked in, Confirmed, Needs follow-up, and Arrived
Unassigned tasks for insurance verification and interpreter confirmation
Privacy reminder and last synchronized time of 08:42

requirements: Associate each appointment with patient, time, clinician, room, visit type, and status
Provide a linear small-screen representation rather than requiring a wide grid
Express status in text and not color alone
Give all static controls appropriate disabled or demonstrative treatment
Use fictional data exactly as supplied and include the privacy reminder
constraints: Do not implement patient search, schedule changes, or new appointments
Do not add diagnoses, contact details, dates of birth, or other sensitive fields
Do not use remote services, images, or fonts
Do not imply that synchronization is live
evaluation_focus: Accessible transformation of a schedule across viewport widths
Clear relationships among appointments, clinicians, rooms, and statuses
